title: Jeow bong (Luang Prabang sweet and spicy chilli paste)

ingredients.name: pork rinds, crushed (a stand-in for the traditional dried buffalo skin)

steps: Toast the dried chillies in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant, then soak them in hot water for 10 minutes.
Grill or dry-roast the shallots, garlic and galangal until charred in places, then peel.
Pound the chillies, shallots, garlic and galangal in a mortar into a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the paste on low heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until deep red and aromatic.
Add the fish sauce, palm sugar and tamarind and simmer for 5 minutes until jam-like, then stir in the pork rinds.
Cool and store in a jar in the fridge for up to a week, serving with sticky rice, vegetables or grilled meat.

title: Jeow mak len (Lao smoky tomato dip)

ingredients.name: sticky rice and raw vegetables, to serve

steps: Grill the whole tomatoes, garlic, shallots and chillies on a hot grill, under an oven grill or in a dry pan, turning, until blackened in spots and soft, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Peel the garlic and shallots, and remove the skin from the tomatoes if it slips off easily.
Pound the garlic, shallots and chillies with the salt in a mortar into a paste.
Add the tomatoes and pound to a chunky, juicy mash, then season with fish sauce.
Stir in the coriander and spring onions and serve with sticky rice, vegetables or grilled meat.

title: Kai yang (Lao grilled chicken with lemongrass and garlic)

ingredients.name: whole chicken, spatchcocked, or bone-in thighs
lime juice, for the dipping sauce
chilli, chopped, for the dipping sauce
sticky rice and green papaya salad, to serve

steps: Pound the lemongrass, garlic and coriander roots and stems into a paste, then mix with 1 tbsp fish sauce, the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar and pepper.
Rub the paste all over the chicken, inside the cuts, and marinate for at least 4 hours in the fridge.
Grill the chicken skin-side down over medium coals, or roast at 200 C, for about 20 minutes, then turn and cook for 20 to 25 minutes more until the skin is golden and the juices run clear.
Rest the chicken for 10 minutes and carve into pieces.
Make the dipping sauce from the remaining fish sauce, lime juice and chilli.
Serve with sticky rice and papaya salad.

title: Keng no mai (Lao bamboo shoot soup)

ingredients.name: boiled bamboo shoots, in thin strips
pork ribs, cut into short pieces
mixed mushrooms (oyster, straw or wood ear)
spinach, pounded with a little water and strained (stand-in for yanang leaf juice)

steps: Boil the bamboo shoots in fresh water for 10 minutes to remove any bitterness, then drain.
Bring the ribs and water to a boil with the lemongrass, skim, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Pound the soaked glutinous rice to a rough paste in a mortar and stir it into the broth to thicken it slightly.
Add the bamboo shoots, pumpkin and mushrooms and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the okra, the spinach liquid, the fish sauce and the chillies and simmer for 5 more minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Serve hot with sticky rice.

title: Khao jee (egg-brushed grilled sticky rice)

ingredients.name: jeow bong or chilli dip, to serve

steps: Drain the soaked rice and steam it in a basket over boiling water for 25 to 30 minutes until tender, tossing once.
Sprinkle the hot rice with salt and mix well.
With wet hands, press a ball of rice about the size of a small fist into a flat, thick oval or wrap it around a skewer.
Grill the rice on a rack over low coals, or in a dry non-stick pan, for 3 to 4 minutes per side until lightly toasted with grill marks.
Brush with beaten egg, return to the heat and cook for another minute per side until the egg is set and golden.
Serve warm with a spicy dip.

title: Khao jee pâté (Lao baguette sandwich)

ingredients.name: cooked ham or Lao-style pork roll

steps: Toss the carrot and daikon with the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt and leave for 20 minutes to lightly pickle, then drain.
Warm the baguettes in a hot oven for 4 to 5 minutes until the crust is crisp.
Split them lengthwise without cutting all the way through, and spread one side with pâté and the other with mayonnaise.
Layer in the ham, cucumber, pickled vegetables and coriander.
Add chilli sauce to taste, press the sandwiches closed, cut in half and serve right away.

title: Khao khua (Lao toasted sticky rice powder)
steps: Place the glutinous rice in a dry wok or heavy frying pan over medium-low heat.
Stir constantly for 12 to 15 minutes until the rice turns deep golden brown and smells nutty. Add the lemongrass and lime leaves for the last 3 minutes if using.
Tip the rice onto a plate and let it cool completely.
Pound it in a mortar or grind in a spice grinder to a coarse, sandy powder.
Store in a jar and use it to thicken and flavour larb, salads and soups.

title: Khao lam (sticky rice with beans roasted in bamboo)

ingredients.name: black-eyed peas or red beans, cooked until nearly tender
bamboo tubes, about 20 cm long, or banana leaves, for wrapping

steps: Drain the soaked rice and mix it with the cooked beans, sugar and salt.
Stir the coconut milk and water together and add enough of it to the rice to just moisten it.
Pack the mixture into the bamboo tubes, leaving a little room at the top, and plug the openings with banana leaf.

Roast the tubes at an angle over low coals or in a 180 C oven, turning, for 40 to 60 minutes, until the rice is cooked through. If you have no bamboo, wrap the mixture in banana leaf parcels and steam for 40 minutes instead.
Let them cool slightly, then split the bamboo or open the parcels and eat the rice in slices or chunks.

title: Khao piak sen (Lao chicken soup with hand-cut noodles)

ingredients.name: garlic, sliced and fried until golden
bean sprouts, lime wedges and chilli, to serve

steps: Simmer the chicken in the water with the galangal, lemongrass and lime leaves for 35 minutes. Lift out the chicken, shred the meat, and keep the broth simmering.
Mix the rice flour and tapioca starch, add the hot water, and knead the warm dough until smooth and elastic.
Roll the dough into ropes and cut into short, thick noodles, dusting them with a little starch so they don't stick.
Drop the noodles into the simmering broth and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring gently, until they float and the broth turns slightly thick and silky.
Season with fish sauce, then ladle into bowls and top with the shredded chicken, fried garlic, spring onions and coriander.
Serve with bean sprouts, lime and chilli.

title: Khao poon (Lao coconut curry noodle soup with chicken)

ingredients.name: shredded cabbage, bean sprouts, mint, basil and lime, to serve

steps: Simmer the chicken in the stock for 25 minutes until cooked through, then lift it out, shred the meat, and keep the stock.
Pound or blend the chillies, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, galangal and 1 lime leaf into a paste.
Fry the paste in a splash of oil for 3 minutes, then stir in the shredded chicken and mash or chop it with the paste.
Add the stock, coconut milk, fish sauce, sugar and the remaining lime leaves and simmer for 15 minutes until slightly thickened and creamy.
Soak the vermicelli in hot water until soft, then drain and divide among four bowls.
Pile on cabbage, sprouts and herbs, ladle over the hot coconut sauce, and serve with lime and chilli flakes.

title: Khao tom (sticky rice and banana parcels)

ingredients.name: banana leaf pieces, about 25 cm, or foil

steps: Drain the rice and combine it with the coconut milk, sugar and salt in a pot. Cook over low heat, stirring, for about 8 minutes until the rice absorbs the milk and becomes sticky but still firm.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water so they bend without tearing.
Spoon a layer of rice onto a leaf, lay a piece of banana (and a few black beans, if using) along the center, and top with more rice.
Fold the leaf into a tight log and tie the ends with string.
Steam the parcels over boiling water for 40 minutes until the rice is soft and sweet.
Cool slightly and serve in the leaf, either warm or at room temperature.

title: Larb (Lao minced meat salad with toasted rice)

ingredients.name: lettuce leaves, raw cabbage and long beans, to serve

steps: Heat a few spoonfuls of water in a pan and cook the minced pork over medium heat, breaking it up, until fully cooked and no pink remains, about 6 to 8 minutes. Take it off the heat and let it cool for a couple of minutes.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice and chilli flakes while the meat is still warm so it absorbs the dressing.
Add the toasted rice powder and mix well; it should lightly coat and bind the meat.
Fold in the shallots, spring onions and most of the herbs.
Taste and adjust, remembering that larb should be sour, salty and spicy in balance.
Serve warm or at room temperature with sticky rice and a platter of raw vegetables and lettuce leaves for scooping.

title: Mee ka tee (Lao coconut noodle soup with minced pork)

ingredients.name: bean sprouts, shredded cabbage, mint, coriander and spring onions, to serve
crushed dried chilli and lime, to serve

steps: Fry the curry paste in a spoon of the thick coconut cream for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook, breaking it up, for 5 minutes until browned.
Pour in the stock and the rest of the coconut cream and simmer for 10 minutes. Season with fish sauce and sugar.
Drizzle the beaten eggs into the simmering soup in a thin stream and let them set into ribbons.
Soak the noodles in hot water until tender, drain, and divide among bowls.
Ladle the soup over, and top with peanuts, sprouts, cabbage and herbs, serving chilli and lime on the side.

title: Or lam (Luang Prabang pork and eggplant stew)

ingredients.name: dried wood ear mushrooms, soaked and torn
Sichuan pepper (stand-in for sakhan, the Lao chilli wood)

steps: Grill or dry-roast the shallots, garlic and chillies until blistered, then pound them with a pinch of salt into a rough paste.
Pound the soaked glutinous rice into a coarse paste; it will thicken the stew.
Simmer the pork in the water with the lemongrass and the roasted paste for 40 minutes until the meat is nearly tender.
Stir in the rice paste, fish sauce and Sichuan pepper and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring so it does not clump.
Add the eggplants, long beans and wood ear mushrooms and cook for 10 to 12 minutes until tender.
Stir in the dill and spring onions, adjust the seasoning, and serve with sticky rice.

title: Sai oua (Lao lemongrass pork sausage)

ingredients.name: kaffir lime leaves, very finely shredded
natural hog casings, rinsed (or shape into patties)

steps: Pound the lemongrass, galangal, shallots, garlic and chillies into a coarse paste.
Mix the paste with the pork, pork fat, lime leaves, fish sauce, salt and sugar, and knead by hand for a few minutes until sticky. Fry a small piece to taste and adjust the seasoning.
Stuff the mixture into the rinsed casings using a sausage stuffer or funnel, and twist into 12 to 15 cm lengths, or shape into thick patties if you have no casings.
Prick the sausages in a few places with a pin.
Grill slowly over medium coals, or bake at 180 C, turning, for 20 to 25 minutes until deeply browned and cooked through with no pink inside.
Serve with sticky rice, fresh herbs and a spicy chilli dip.

title: Seen savanh (sweet Lao beef jerky with sesame)

ingredients.name: lean beef (top round or flank), sliced as thinly as possible against the grain

steps: Mix the fish sauce, oyster sauce, palm sugar, garlic, ginger, lemongrass, chilli and sesame seeds, and coat the beef slices well. Marinate in the fridge overnight.
Lay the beef in a single layer on wire racks set over baking trays.
Dry in a very low oven at 80 C for 2.5 to 3 hours, turning once, until the slices are dark and leathery but not brittle.
Let the dried strips cool and rest for an hour.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the strips for 30 to 60 seconds per side until sizzling and slightly crisp at the edges, and hot all the way through.
Serve warm with sticky rice and a chilli dip.

title: Soup no mai (Lao bamboo shoot salad)

ingredients.name: pork skin or pork belly, boiled and sliced (optional)

steps: Blanch the shredded bamboo shoots in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and squeeze out the water.
Mix the fish sauce, lime juice and chilli flakes in a large bowl.
Add the bamboo shoots, shallots and optional pork, and toss to coat.
Stir in the toasted rice powder so it clings to the shoots.
Fold in the spring onions and herbs, taste for balance, and serve with sticky rice.

title: Tam mak hoong (Lao green papaya salad)

ingredients.name: long beans, cut into 4 cm pieces
sticky rice and raw vegetables, to serve

steps: Pound the garlic and chillies together in a large mortar until roughly crushed.
Add the palm sugar, fish sauce and lime juice and stir to dissolve.
Add the long beans and bruise them lightly with the pestle.
Add the shredded papaya and tomatoes and pound gently while turning with a spoon, just enough to bruise the papaya and let it take up the dressing.
Taste for a balance of salty, sour, sweet and hot, scatter the peanuts on top and serve immediately with sticky rice.
